neighbours.label: a noun naming harm or ruin in a frame of escaping, averting or repairing it (deliver us from evil, not all doom and gloom, windshield repair, mitigating damage); neutral nouns in the same frames stay low
fire: The priest asked God to protect the village from harm and from evil.
Sales are down this quarter, but it is not all doom and despair.
The shop on Main Street does bumper repair and dent removal.
New levees should help mitigate flood damage along the river.
The charm was meant to ward off evil from the newborn child.
Volunteers worked through the night to rescue families from disaster.
The airbag is designed to reduce injuries in a crash.
The vaccine program aims to prevent illness and death in the elderly.
quiet: The priest asked God to bless the village and the harvest.
Sales are up this quarter, and everyone is pleased with the results.
The shop on Main Street sells bumper stickers and postcards.
New levees will be built along the river next year.
The charm was a gift from the grandmother of the newborn child.
Volunteers worked through the night to paint the community hall.
The airbag is stored in the centre of the steering wheel.
The vaccine program is run by nurses in the town clinic.
